Phaedrus stood at the edge of a crystalline forest, frozen in awe at what he saw. Here, there was a great act of destruction that glassed the face of Gaea, and yet here too there was new life.

*The gods,* Phaedrus reflected, *Are fickle beings indeed.*

Phaedrus had contemplated much at the Stone of Reflection. He knew every idea that spawned from it was his own, it could only have been, it will always be. Yet they were not his thoughts, they felt foreign, as if they did not belong. He knew there were many that he could not remember, some surface, now and then, but most stayed hidden under the haze of recollection. Ideas barely half formed still swam in the back of his mind, and only with a sudden burst of clarity, or a the sight of an unique phenomenon, did the idea explode into clarity and consciousness, becoming remembered once more.

This was one of those moments. In a single moment, Phaedrus understood everything, then his mind collapsed back down and he returned, with two new ideas fully formed, fully remembered.

The gods were caring, they were uncaring. They were kind and unkind. Creators, yet destroyers. A strange dichotomy, shared amongst many divinities.

Similarly, there exists creation in destruction. With destruction comes the potential to begin again, creating something new, perhaps even something greater. The very world seems to operate in a strange dichotomy that was hopelessly intertwined. A curious development and a curious thought, but not altogether an important one. Here, in the forest of reflection, the crystals lived, even though they were born from destruction. They breathed, even as the creation of the scar took the last breath of many individuals caught in the blast.

Yet on that breath was the promise of a great power, the crystals lived, they directed. Inside them there was flow, flow of power, of magic. The winds whispered, and through the Crystal Forest, the magic found itself trapped into a great glade. The very structure of the crystals shaped the flow into channels. It was the same information that Perditaj had yielded, but Phaedrus did not understand. Standing in the clear glade, Phaedrus saw it now.

Magic flowed in pathways, it was channeled through structures. The structure gave it purpose and direction. Here, in the Crystal Trees, there was structure, and power flowed through every channel, down from every branch, and into the earth.

To master the creation of floatstone, the gem must be structured to fly, it must have the will to sustain flight, and the imagination to convert the energies floating upon the wind into force. All this Phaedrus had done without understanding. His inventions had been crude, unwieldy. They lacked flexibility, for there was only one pathway. They lacked adaptability, for they had no understanding of flight and no sense of direction.

For the control he desired, he knew how the floatstone must be made, and he knew that something else must control it.

In the reflection of the Forest of Reflection lay the City of Crystal, Sentenza. Its central tower looming proudly over the horizon, thinking, understanding, directing. A great hub, involving great sacrifice. It was by all rights just a building, but it moved and lived just the same. Luminus had sacrificed everything, even his very life, yet even in death he lived on, a guiding light for the Spectra, a director for all their communications. He was diminished by the sacrifice, yet he was also more. There could be others, other crystals, lesser perhaps, but made for a different purpose. A living, thinking crystal. Dead stone brought to life.

Phaedrus smiled, sometimes, knowledge came from the outside, but it was artificial and false, it is knowledge that you wield, like a blade. You may possess it, but it isn't yours. The greatest knowledge came from reflection, it is a part of you, like a limb. You observe, and you could see a truth, but a truth is not understanding. Knowledge comes when the truths are connected, when observations become tied together.

*True Knowledge comes from Within.* Phaedrus muttered. *Take what you see, and make it your own.*

Phaedrus rose, and returned on the long tract back to the city that he called home.

Phaedrus reflects in the Forest of Reflection, and returns from the Stone of Knowledge. He realizes the contradiction that is present in many things and realizes the error of his previous research. He takes the new ideas and returns to Sentenza.
